identity.name: Living Vrindavan
identity.purpose: Living Vrindavan is a persistent experiential world inspired by Vrindavan in the Krishna tradition. It is not intended merely as a digital reconstruction of a historical or mythological place. It is a living environment through which the participant encounters themes of joy, love, relationship, play, nature, attention, surrender, and belonging.

locations.name: Vrindavan Entry
locations.purpose: The participant crosses from ordinary experience into Living Vrindavan. This location establishes presence and orientation rather than challenge.
locations.humanQuestion: What changes when you arrive without needing to achieve anything?

locations.name: Yamuna
locations.purpose: Yamuna represents movement, relationship, continuity, and the possibility of allowing experience to move rather than controlling it.
locations.humanQuestion: What becomes visible when you stop trying to control the current?

locations.name: Kadamba Grove
locations.role: Grove / intimacy with the living environment
locations.purpose: Kadamba Grove represents attention to life at close range: sound, movement, shade, texture, presence, play, and relationship.
locations.humanQuestion: What do you notice when nothing is asking for your attention?

locations.name: Govardhan Path
locations.purpose: Govardhan Path introduces movement through the world and the relationship between joy, responsibility, protection, community, and action.
locations.humanQuestion: What becomes worth carrying when it is carried for more than yourself?
